history.summary: No CSV town/district/state correction needed: the temple is at Old Daily Market, Marwari Patti, Dimapur 797112, Dimapur district, Nagaland (map coordinates 25.90427, 93.72535 match the published location). This is the best-documented Hindu temple in Dimapur: inheritage.foundation's Bengal-architecture survey describes it as built in the latter half of the 20th century by the sizeable Bengali community of Dimapur, a two-storied concrete edifice (ground floor sanctum sanctorum, upper floor community hall used during festivals) with brightly painted deity depictions and floral motifs reminiscent of Kolkata Durga Puja pandals, carrying a distinct flavour of Bengal's Durga Puja festivities with a subtle Naga undercurrent (earthen lamps in the courtyard, mixed Bengali-Naga congregation). It carries a 4.2/5 rating from 121 reviews on Yappe.in and sits about 3.5 km from Dimapur railway station, beside a vegetable/fruit bazaar and food stalls. Do not conflate with the separate 'Shri Shri Durga/Shiv Mandir' at Duncan Basti (also listed in Dimapur), the Kalibari at Kalibari Road, or Durga temples across the Assam border (Diphu/Sarupathar listings).

name: Durga Mandir
town_description: Dimapur is Nagaland's largest city and commercial gateway, lying in the foothills at the state's southwestern edge on the border with Assam. The only Nagaland city with a railway station and airport, it is the natural base for the state's small Hindu community (mostly Bengali, Nepali, Assamese, Marwari and Hindi-speaking settlers), whose temples cluster in areas like Marwari Patti, Old Daily Market, Railway Colony and Signal Bosti.

travel.airport: Dimapur Airport (DMU), approx. 7-10 km from the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Dimapur railway station approx. 3.5 km away (per Yappe.in); auto-rickshaws and taxis available.
travel.road: At Old Daily Market, Marwari Patti, in central Dimapur; easily reachable by auto-rickshaw/taxi within town (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Durga Puja/Navratri (September-October) is the temple's most important festival period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify - confirm locally before visiting). No entry fee expected; the surrounding Old Daily Market bazaar is liveliest in the evenings.
